and key learning points (prefinal examination)"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EFollowing the case discussion of a \u003Cu\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/chandanatallamraj.blogspot.com\/2023\/12\/blog-post.html\"\u003E60 year old female\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E who presented with active uncontrolled abnormal movements of the limbs, some questions which were discussed as part of the Objective Structured Clinical Examination are:\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1. What triggers Status epilepticus in a patient with pre-existing epilepsy?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u003Ci\u003EThere are many etiologies for status epilepticus including both obvious causes like non-compliance with the prescribed anti-epileptic medication (To be noted: the medication prescribed in the past for this patient was chronically underdosed) and other causes like:\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cul style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003ECerebrovascular\u0026nbsp;accidents\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003ECentral nervous system infections\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EDrug withdrawal syndromes (alcohol, benzodiazepines)\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EMetabolic derangements (hypoglycemia)\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EHypoxia\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EHead trauma\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EHypertensive emergencies\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EAutoimmune disorders\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EIn this patient it was noted that at the time of admission, patient had hyperglycemia (GRBS: 222mg\/dL) which later normalized without the need for medical intervention.\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; font-size: large; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEh7dhxUnQLoUzTwUKNjG5v-jkZ0GxqX9oW3-_YCMwCF22awxywl9ZMpDHDsc8HH9PALKHYmR0m-K9shwSTR0IlMpt6sOjZ9NxPC-S9K40xjrbDCbMHPws9x_acibHzcA4kKu5GTMgZMAFBTIyPxPli9ijqk-9jB2go2C1GTaYmVwsirDLCxKdhYRCNX8p8\/s1024\/GRBS%20on%20admission.jpg\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"1024\" data-original-width=\"1006\" height=\"320\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEh7dhxUnQLoUzTwUKNjG5v-jkZ0GxqX9oW3-_YCMwCF22awxywl9ZMpDHDsc8HH9PALKHYmR0m-K9shwSTR0IlMpt6sOjZ9NxPC-S9K40xjrbDCbMHPws9x_acibHzcA4kKu5GTMgZMAFBTIyPxPli9ijqk-9jB2go2C1GTaYmVwsirDLCxKdhYRCNX8p8\/s320\/GRBS%20on%20admission.jpg\" width=\"314\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; font-size: large; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: large; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EThe next question then becomes: \u003Cu\u003ECan hyperglycemia can be the cause of status epilepticus\u003C\/u\u003E?\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-size: large; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121; font-family: Cambria, \u0026quot;Cambria Math\u0026quot;, stixgeneral, \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, Times, serif;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\"Hyperglycemia-induced seizures are refractory to antiepileptic medications, account for 15–40% of seizures in patients with HHS, and are commonly focal motor seizures and epilepsia partialis continua\" according to an \u003Cu\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/scholar.google.com\/scholar_lookup?journal=Neurology\u0026amp;title=Focal+seizures+as+a+manifestation+of+hyperglycemia+without+ketoacidosis.+A+report+of+seven+cases+with+review+of+the+literature\u0026amp;author=M+Maccario\u0026amp;author=CP+Messis\u0026amp;author=EF+Vastola\u0026amp;volume=15\u0026amp;publication_year=1965\u0026amp;pages=195-206\u0026amp;pmid=14262318\u0026amp;\"\u003Earticle\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EHowever, HHS or Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State is a life threatening complication of diabetes mellitus and this patient is not a known case of diabetes mellitus.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EThe question remains about the exact etiology of this particular episode of seizure that the patient presented with.\u003Cspan\u003E\u003Ca name='more'\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E2. Comment on the therapeutic index of Phenytoin. In this case, can the fact that the anti-epileptic medication was chronically underdosed be considered medical malpractice?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EAccording to another article published by \u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC4140577\/\"\u003ENational Institutes of Health\u003C\/a\u003E, Phenytoin is classified as a NTI(Narrow Therapeutic Index) drug.\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EThis means that the efficacy of Phenytoin as an anti-epileptic drug is limited to a narrow blood concentration beyond which it is lethal and below which it is ineffective. This explains why the patient kept experiencing seizure episodes over the years despite taking Phenytoin religiously for the past 23 years.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cu\u003EUnderdosing could be the cause of persistence of the seizures\u003C\/u\u003E. In addition, the long term use of Phenytoin has led to Grade one drug-induced gingival overgrowth (\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK538518\/#article-34282.r4\"\u003EDIGO\u003C\/a\u003E) in the patient.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EIn conclusion, Yes. The long term underdosing of Phenytoin to treat a case of epilepsy can very well be considered medical malpractice. Vigilance in the practice of prescribing drugs must be effected and drug dosages must be tailored to meet the specific needs of each patient.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EFurthermore, patients on long term medications must be encouraged to go to their clinician for regular follow ups to be monitored for adverse affects and treated appropriately.\u003Cspan\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C!--more--\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: large;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E3. Is central IV access necessary for managing a patient with epilepsy?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: large;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EIV access is crucial for treating epilepsy, especially in acute conditions like status epilepticus when IV Benzodiazepines are to be given immediately after admission.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EHowever, once the patient has been stabilized, the question arises about the duration of maintenance\u0026nbsp;of central IV line due to the risk of infections and\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003Ethrombophlebitis.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EIn yet another article published by the \u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC8160666\/\"\u003ENational Institutes of Health'\u003C\/a\u003E\u0026nbsp;the results of several randomized clinical trials, cohort studies, case and control studies, descriptive and qualitative studies have indicated the following steps as sufficient to prevent phlebitis:\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cul style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cu\u003EProtocol monitoring and continuous evaluation\u003C\/u\u003E: Records that show date of puncture, dressings used, professional performing the procedure, puncture locations, number of puncture attempts and such.\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cu\u003EAsepsis\u003C\/u\u003E: Using alcoholic chlorhexidine at \u0026gt;0.5% or aqueous chlorhexidine at 2%. In case of hypersensitivity, iodine solution or 70% alcohol may be used.\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cu\u003EInvolving the patient:\u003C\/u\u003E\u0026nbsp;in the choice of PVC (Peripheral Venous Catheter) and puncture site. Analyzing patient characteristics, medication prescribed, expected duration of treatment and other risk factors before opting a PVC.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cu\u003EDressing\u003C\/u\u003E: It is not advisable to bandage the site of the IV line. A sterile, transparent, semipermeable adhesive dressing may be used to improve visibility at the puncture site.\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cu\u003ENursing interventions to treat phlebitis\u003C\/u\u003E: Application of alternate hot and cold compresses to decrease edema, erythema and pain is advised. Other non pharmacological substances like sesame oil or chamomile extract maybe used in small amounts to provide relief to the patient.\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan\u003E\u003C!--more--\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E4. Why was Ceftrioxone administered to this patient?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EThe patient was given Ceftriaxone prophylactically to prevent infections.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Ci style=\"font-size: large;\"\u003EHowever, according to a \u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/2925456\/\"\u003Estudy done in 103 male patients\u003C\/a\u003E undergoing transurethral surgery who were given Ceftriaxone as the sole antimicrobial, the drug was not particularly useful beyond the immediate post-operative period.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EIn contrast, according to a certain \u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.sciencedirect.com\/science\/article\/abs\/pii\/S0735675720301649\"\u003Eother retrospective study\u003C\/a\u003E, IV 1g of Ceftriaxone is recommended to be administered over at least 30 minutes. The total adverse event rate observed was 1 in 753 cases or 0.13%.\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003EThus, it can be left to the attending physician's discretion whether to administer the prophylactic dose of Ceftrioxone or not. The physician is expected to keep in mind patient characteristics, drug interactions and other risk factors while making a decision.\u003Cspan\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C!--more--\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Ch4 style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EKEY LEARNING POINTS\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/h4\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Col style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EIn studying the management of this patient as part of the OSCE, I have learnt the value of doing the due diligence of looking up the latest research before administering any drug to patients, preferably on a regular basis.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EThe importance of doctors working as a team with nurses, paramedics and other hospital technicians to ensure smooth sailing of patient management and to avoid unnecessary confusion.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EDocumentation of every patient encounter on all levels (medical student, intern, post graduate, senior resident, and professor) with proper integration and regular case discussions, if done in a systematic and well-structured manner, can improve the quality of health care significantly even in rural settings.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EThe vertical and horizontal integration of medical subjects (General medicine with pathology and pharmacology, etc.) as prescribed by NMC, India is practically applicable and absolutely necessary for every medical student in order to increase the competence of future doctors.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EManaging or assisting in the management of real-time patients and retrospective reviews are the two most effective methods to understand and practice clinical medicine.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan\u003E\u003C!--more--\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ol\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cbr Patient has been on \u003Cu\u003Eanticonvulsive medication since the past 23 years.\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EA \u003Cu\u003Etypical episode\u003C\/u\u003E begins with headache and dizziness, up-rolling of the eyes followed by loss of consciousness and uncontrolled involuntary movements of the arms and legs, clasping of the hands and deviation of the mouth to one side. Frothing and tongue bite was seen in the initial years. She usually regains consciousness 5-10 minutes later in a confused state, with no memory of the episode. There have been instances of falling to the floor when no one was around to help her. The precipitating factors for such episodes were emotional distress and\/or lack of sleep.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EThe \u003Cu\u003Ecurrent episode\u003C\/u\u003E began in the morning time, when the patient was on an empty stomach and complained that she felt uneasy. She also had a right sided headache of dragging type, radiating to her neck. This was followed by up-rolling of the eyes, clasping of the hands,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan\u003Eloss of consciousness,\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan\u003E\u0026nbsp;and involuntary movements of the limbs which did not subside even after 30 minutes.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan
